scope: the Allegrex executable of the pinned USA disc
provenance: No toolchain has been qualified yet. The PS2 siblings could not use a modern GCC for the R5900 either, and they solved it by measuring the register mode of the target; the Allegrex case has to be measured the same way, and it has not been.

candidates.provenance: The GCC toolchain built for the Allegrex (PSP), as used by the PSPSDK and by the homebrew toolchains. An external binary: pinned by hash, never rebuilt here, never committed.
candidates.notes: The PSP SDK defaults are -O2 -G0. The retail build used its own flags, which are unknown; they are part of what phase 2 has to establish.

candidates.kind: Allegrex MIPS cross compiler from the PSPSDK
candidates.provenance: The PSPSDK toolchain, the one the game was most likely built with. An external binary: pinned by hash, never rebuilt here, never committed.
candidates.notes: Closer in spirit to the retail build than a modern GNU toolchain, and therefore the more likely first candidate to measure.

candidates.provenance: The Allegrex static-recompilation toolkits: sp00nznet/psprecomp, wizardengineer/psprecomp and the psprism toolchain of anthonyhfm/psprism.
candidates.notes: These recompile rather than decompile. They are the right family of tools for the portability goal, and the wrong tool for the matching goal; they are listed because the project may deliver both, and because the recompilation route is what makes the game playable without the hardware.

notes: This file records the *candidates* and the evidence each one would need. It does not record a qualified toolchain, because there is none yet: the executable behind the ~PSP container has not been read, so no compiler output can be compared with anything.
